messages:
ana: hi all, ana here — first week on infra. my Buildkite pipeline runs but the final publish step errors out when pushing to ghcr.io: `denied: requested access to the resource is denied`. unsure if this is a perms issue or a secret naming mismatch.
josh: welcome! :wave: can you paste the publish step and the env name you set in Buildkite?
ana: i set a secret at the pipeline level called `REG_TOKEN`. publish step is: 
```
- name: Publish
  command: |
    docker build -t ghcr.io/redwood-inference/service:${BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER} .
    echo "$REG_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u $GH_USER --password-stdin
    docker push ghcr.io/redwood-inference/service:${BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER}
```
ana: logs show docker login succeeds but push gets denied.
maya: two common issues: 1) GHCR requires the token to have write:packages and read:packages sometimes; 2) org SSO can block the token. what is $GH_USER set to?
ana: $GH_USER is my GH handle (ana-dev). i was able to `docker login` locally with a PAT but pushes still failed.
ci-bot: Buildkite build #102 failed 4 publish-image (exit code 1).
josh: if login succeeds but push is denied, likely the token doesn't have packages:write or the repo package permissions aren't granted to that user/machine account. also if the token is a GitHub App token it won't work; PAT is fine but SSO matters.
nana: what's the recommended pattern? i saw other repos use `redwood-ci-deploy` machine user.
maya: we prefer a machine user for GHCR pushes. we create `redwood-ci-deploy`, grant it Packages->Write on the repo/org, generate a PAT, and add it as `GHCR_PAT` to the pipeline (masked, pipeline env). Buildkite prefer `GHCR_PAT`; GitHub Actions workflows expect `GHCR_TOKEN` usually.
nana: ah i used `REG_TOKEN` and `GH_USER` which is probably why the workflow isn't wired for rotation.
gha-bot: GitHub Actions run 201 failed (publish job) 4 see run https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/actions/runs/201
josh: i'll create the machine user and add the token. also double-check the repo has the package namespace enabled and the package visibility allows writes from the machine user.
maya: note: if your personal account is enforced by SSO, your PAT might be blocked; that's why machine user tokens are easier for CI.
josh: created `redwood-ci-deploy`, granted packages:write on the repo, created PAT, added `GHCR_PAT` to Buildkite pipeline and `GHCR_TOKEN` to repo secrets for actions. also installed the Buildkite GitHub App on the repo.
ci-bot: Buildkite build #103 started (branch: onboarding/ana-first-build).
nana: build 103 4 passed! woo. two quick questions: 1) where's the concise note on secret naming + SSO gotchas? 2) who owns rotating the machine token?
maya: doc is `docs/dev/onboarding/ci.md` and `docs/dev/ci-secrets.md` — open a PR if anything missing. rotations: infra schedules rotations quarterly but ops owns the rotation process; tag @josh for repo-specific updates. we'll add a short SSO note to the onboarding doc.
nana: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick help. i'll add a short sentence to the onboarding doc about GHCR token naming. :tada:
josh: welcome aboard! ping me if you want a quick walkthrough of the pipeline steps later today.
